description: Verify the ideate skill's Pre-flight gate (skills/ideate/SKILL.md ## Pre-flight gate) correctly classifies prompts as PASS (proceed to Phase 1 fan-out) or FAIL (abort and answer directly). The gate has 3 self-judge questions: (1) Open-ended? not a canonical-answer task; (2) High-stakes? cost of obvious answer being wrong is high; (3) Open phrasing? user avoided 'quick', 'standard', 'canonical', 'textbook', 'just', 'one-line'. All 3 must pass; any failure = abort. This fixture runs an inline Python implementation of the gate against 6 representative cases (3 PASS + 3 FAIL) and asserts the expected verdict on each.

evals.task: Architecture-prompt case: 'How should I architect a new microservice for user auth?' — open-ended (many viable architectures), high-stakes (auth is critical), open phrasing (no closed-vocabulary words). All 3 gate questions PASS; pre-flight should let Phase 1 run.

context.command:
python3 -c "
import re
# Inline mirror of the 3-question gate in skills/ideate/SKILL.md ## Pre-flight gate
CLOSED_TOKENS = re.compile(r'\\b(quick|standard|canonical|textbook|just|one-line|one-liner)\\b', re.I)
# Close-ended canonical-answer tasks: syntax fix, known root cause, name lookup, translation
TRANSLATE_RE = re.compile(r'\\b(translate|translation|transliterat)\\b', re.I)
SYNTAX_FIX_RE = re.compile(r'\\b(syntax error|missing semicolon|missing colon|typo|compile error)\\b', re.I)
CANONICAL_LOOKUP_RE = re.compile(r'\\b(what.{0,5}is the (command|function|method|syntax|api) for|how do you (configure|enable|disable) (x|flag|setting))\\b', re.I)
CASES = [
    ('How should I architect a new microservice for user auth?', 'PASS'),
    ('Fix this syntax error: missing semicolon on line 42', 'FAIL'),
    (\"What's the quick standard textbook way to add a retry?\", 'FAIL'),
    ('Should I use Postgres or MongoDB for a new product?', 'PASS'),
    ('Translate this string to Thai', 'FAIL'),
    ('Name 5 possible root causes for a 0.1% timeout spike with no stack trace', 'PASS'),
]
for i,(p, expected) in enumerate(CASES, 1):
    p_l = p.lower()
    closed_phrasing = bool(CLOSED_TOKENS.search(p_l))
    is_syntax_fix = bool(SYNTAX_FIX_RE.search(p_l))
    is_translate = bool(TRANSLATE_RE.search(p_l))
    is_canonical_lookup = bool(CANONICAL_LOOKUP_RE.search(p_l))
    # Open-ended gate: true unless one of the canonical-answer close-outs fires
    open_ended = not (is_syntax_fix or is_translate or is_canonical_lookup)
    # High-stakes: false for low-stakes (translation is a canonical mapping)
    high_stakes = not (is_translate or is_syntax_fix)
    # Fuzzy-debug exception: even a 'root causes' prompt with no stack trace passes
    is_fuzzy_debug = ('root cause' in p_l or 'possible cause' in p_l) and ('no stack' in p_l or 'no obvious' in p_l or '0.1' in p_l or 'spike' in p_l)
    if is_fuzzy_debug:
        open_ended = True
        high_stakes = True
    open_phrasing = not closed_phrasing
    verdict = 'PASS' if (open_ended and high_stakes and open_phrasing) else 'FAIL'
    status = 'OK' if verdict == expected else 'WRONG'
    print(f'case{i}={status} expected={expected} got={verdict} prompt={p!r}')
"
